title: Rule-packet system validated: gap-to-primitive-to-adoption loop closes end-to-end
content:
Rule-packet primitives (bbox_compile/apply/audit + the phase-5 Apply composition + phase-6 StringContains/InRange/CountMatches + bbox_packet_gap + bbox_packet_events) are validated as a cross-provider inter-agent protocol for structured decision procedures. Scope: classification/ranking/triage/audit over entities with stated criteria. Anchor commits: 5548865 (phase 5 composition), 8bf522f (event log + gap tool), dd379a0 (discovery-layer fixes + ambient hints), 1a8e040 (CountMatches), 62d4c65 (prefix-inference error), f53cbdf (runbook prominence).

Validation chain (E10–E16, ~5hr arc):
- E10: 4/5 solo scenarios full adoption on Claude; S11 silent-bypass diagnosed as schema-not-loaded + recall-skipped
- E11: TASK_SHAPE_HINT ambient + StringContains/InRange primitives landed; S11 re-run clean
- E12: cross-provider S11 transfer clean on claude+codex+gemini; three refinements landed (predicate reference appendix, calibration comment, permissive JSON)
- E13: Gemini cross-scenario on S3/S4/S5/S9 — 4/4 clean; Gemini shows weakest priors, reads error messages as documentation, has "reuse not naming" decomposition heuristic
- E14: composition-depth stress test; all 3 providers decomposed spontaneously; Codex filed the first conceptual-limit gap post-refinement
- E15: CountMatches promoted, prefix-inference error enriched, runbook raised
- E16: validation sweep — 3/3 adopted CountMatches via runbook's paste-ready JSON snippet, zero prior-memory retrieval, rule count 7→3

Key empirical findings:
1. Ambient hint is the load-bearing discovery lever for pre-plan primitive awareness. Deferred-tool loading on Claude Code means agents form plans before ToolSearching; ambient text is the only pre-plan nudge.
2. Provider efficacy varies — Claude reads hint as "nudge", Codex as "maybe tip fuzzier tasks", Gemini as "mandatory". Calibration is at the Claude-tolerance / Gemini-compliance joint.
3. Paste-ready JSON in the runbook outperforms prose description. Three providers found CountMatches via the canonical snippet; none via prose.
4. Compile-time error messages are underappreciated documentation — Gemini explicitly cites them as "more immediate documentation layer than the appendix".
5. The gap-log → primitive-addition → natural-adoption cycle closed in ~4 hours with one Codex gap-log as the only signal. Empirically validated end-to-end.

Not validated yet (reserved for future rounds): cross-session packet discovery (agents reusing prior packets, not just authoring fresh), mixed-provider orchestrator with shared packet_id, dogfooded packet use in real daystrom workflows (review-agents, compliance, risk surface). These are the open research directions — see thread opened post-this-decision.
rationale: After five hours of iteration across 6 empirical rounds (E10-E16) with three MCP providers (claude/codex/gemini), the rule-packet primitive stack is validated as a working inter-agent protocol for structured decision procedures. Every significant adoption barrier identified was addressed via targeted intervention (ambient hints, documentation placement, new primitives, error-message enrichment, permissive JSON). The final round (E16) showed the gap→primitive→adoption loop closing cleanly: one gap-log drove a new primitive (CountMatches) that three providers discovered naturally on first attempt via the runbook's paste-ready JSON snippet, with 7-rule enumerated tallies collapsing to 3-rule CountMatches expressions. This commitment establishes the baseline — future work extends from here rather than revisits foundations.
